subject: AI & Agents
title: A/B Testing: The Real-World Scorecard
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: A/B Testing: The Real-World Scorecard.

hook.text: Your model beats the baseline in the lab. But does it actually improve the user experience? A/B test it.

buildup.text: A/B testing shows the old model to half the users and the new model to the other half.

discovery.text: You measure real outcomes — clicks, purchases, satisfaction — not just prediction accuracy.

twist.text: Sometimes a more accurate model hurts user experience. People don't always want optimal recommendations.

climax.text: Google runs thousands of A/B tests per year. Every search change is validated this way.

punchline.text: The only metric that matters is impact in the real world.

quiz.question: Why do companies A/B test AI models?
options: To measure real-world impact, not just lab accuracy

details.summary: A/B testing compares two versions of a system on real users to measure which performs better. It is the gold standard for evaluating AI in production because lab performance does not always match the real world.
details.whyItMatters: A model that looks great on benchmarks might fail with real users. A/B testing provides ground truth about real-world performance, preventing costly mistakes from deploying inferior systems.
takeaways: A/B tests compare versions using real user interactions
Lab benchmarks often do not predict real-world performance well
Statistical rigor prevents drawing conclusions from noise

faq.question: How does A/B testing work for AI models?
faq.answer: Users are randomly split into groups. Group A sees the current model and Group B sees the new model. Real metrics like engagement, accuracy, and revenue are compared. Statistical tests determine if differences are real.

faq.question: How long should an A/B test run?
faq.answer: Until you have enough data for statistical significance — usually thousands of observations minimum. Running too short risks false conclusions. The exact duration depends on traffic volume and the size of the expected effect.
